subject: Private deployment data governance Q&A - residency, retention, deletion
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Beckett <t.beckett@corpsec.com>; Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data residency & deletion for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo today — Acme is seriously considering Redwood Private for a PHI-adjacent pilot. Before we move to procurement, our security and legal teams asked for a short Q&A on the following:

- Can you confirm that customer data (inputs and generated outputs) remains only inside our VPC and chosen cloud region (no replication outside region)?
- What is Redwood's standard retention policy for logs, backups, and snapshots created by the service in Private deployments?
- If we request deletion of a customer workspace, what is the technical process and SLA for permanent purge (including backups and snapshot copies)?
- Do you provide proof-of-deletion / attestation suitable for audits?
- Can we use our own KMS/HSM so Redwood never has key access?

We need clear answers for our procurement questionnaire. If you can share a short runbook and any sample contract clauses it would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Asha
Security Liaison, Acme Health
(appearance: attachment: PHI-compliance-requirements.pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on data residency & deletion for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Asha — great meeting earlier. Short answers up front, details below and Marissa (security/compliance) is copied with the deep dive.

- Residency: Yes — in Redwood Private deployed into your VPC we do not replicate customer workspace blobs outside the selected region unless explicitly configured (discussed in the architecture section below).
- Retention: Default is configurable; typical defaults are 30 days for transient logs, 90 days for operational traces, and customer-configurable retention for persistent artifacts.
- Deletion: We support immediate workspace purge + background scrub for snapshots/backups; target purge SLA is 7 days for full irreversible deletion, can be shortened in contract.
- Proof: We can provide deletion attestations and audit logs (signed entries) and include deletion clauses in contract.
- KMS/HSM: Supported — you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with a customer-managed KMS; Redwood runs with envelope encryption so we never have plaintext keys.

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-data-handling-brief.pdf (summary), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Next steps: Marissa, can you add the step-by-step runbook and a typical sample clause for procurement?

Best,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on data residency & deletion for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Asha — adding a technical runbook and Q&A. Long version below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR:
- Customer data and derived artifacts live in customer-controlled storage within your VPC and region; control plane (optional) can be run in a separate management VPC or as a hosted control plane depending on your procurement.
- BYOK via customer KMS/HSM supported (no Redwood access to key material).
- Deletion is a two-step process: 1) immediate workspace detach + metadata tombstone, 2) background purge that removes blobs, snapshots, and rotates pointers. Standard contract SLA: irreversible purge within 7 days; expedited 48-hour option available with enterprise addendum.
- We emit signed audit records and offer signed deletion attestations (PDF) that include checksums of removed manifests.

Detailed runbook (high level):
1) Customer initiates delete via Console API or CLI (DELETE /v1/workspaces/:id) while authenticated via your IdP.
2) Redwood control plane marks workspace as DELETING and emits an audit event to the customer-defined audit sink (syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver).
3) Primary blob deletion: objects stored in customer-managed buckets (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) are removed via strong delete operation (delete + overwrite window if configured).
4) Snapshot/backup handling: automated snapshots are cataloged in a snapshot index; deletion schedules trigger snapshot expunge workers that remove snapshot objects and clear the index entry.
5) Offsite/backups: by default Redwood Private does not copy workspace blobs to external regions. If cross-region replication is enabled for your resilience policy, deletion will trigger replication invalidation and coordinated purge across replicas.
6) Index/log purge: operational logs retained per your configured retention; logs containing PII/PHI can be redacted prior to ingestion on request.
7) Finalization: once objects are removed, the control plane rotates object manifests and publishes a signed deletion attestation containing a list of removed object keys and checksums.

Key technical controls and guarantees:
- Storage residency: storage endpoints are bound to the cloud region specified in deployment template; control plane operations that would move data outside the region require an explicit configuration flag and customer approval.
- BYOK/KMS: Redwood supports customer-supplied KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations via KMIP for on-prem HSMs. Redwood only holds envelope-wrapped keys and cannot decrypt without customer permission.
- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are stored as objects in the same bucket/region; default snapshot retention is configurable. We provide an optional setting to disable snapshots entirely for regulated workloads.
- Immutable backups / legal hold: If your legal team requires immutable retention, we can configure WORM-style buckets but that will prevent deletion until the hold expires — we flag this as a tradeoff.
- Proof-of-deletion: attestations include signed manifests; for higher assurance we support an auditor-facing audit log stream or an on-site verification run with signed runbook outputs.
- SLA timings: standard deletion purge window 7 days; enterprise expedited 48 hours; emergency purge can be negotiated.
- Operational logs: default redwood runtime logs kept for 90 days; you may configure shorter windows or ship logs off-platform immediately to your SIEM.

Known caveats and recommendations:
- If you enable cross-region replication for disaster recovery, coordinate the deletion window across replicas — this may extend purge time unless replication invalidation is configured.
- Third-party backups (customer-managed archival) are outside Redwood purview; ensure your archival policies are aligned.
- For complete no-exfil guarantee, use a Private/on-prem package and BYOK with strict IAM and no egress rules for the admin network.

Attachments in this email: sample runbook excerpts and the SOC2 summary we previously attached.

If it helps, Karthik can share sample contract language and a DocuSign template.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-private-vpc-data-handling-brief.pdf)

Thanks Marissa — that clarifies a lot. A few follow-ups before we move to an internal approval: 

1) Backups & archival: if we have a compliance requirement to retain a limited set of artifacts for 2 years, can we configure Redwood to persist only a policy-limited subset while ensuring everything else is purged? How do you scope the subset?
2) Proof for auditors: can you provide an example deletion attestation (redacted is fine) and what the attestation cryptographic signature looks like?
3) Contract SLA: our procurement wants the 48-hour expedited deletion in writing and a sample clause. Will that be a chargeable add-on?
4) Logs: we prefer logs to be forwarded to our SIEM within 24 hours and purged from Redwood storage after 7 days. Is that feasible?

Could we put a short call on calendar (ops + security + procurement) to finalize the runbook and contract language?

Best,
Asha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@acmehealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on data residency & deletion for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Asha — short answers and I've attached sample contract language.

1) Backups & archival: Yes — we support retention policies that tag snapshots for "long-term retention". You can scope retention by dataset tags (e.g., "compliance:retain"), by workspace, or by object prefix. We recommend scoping at object prefix/metadata level to keep control fine-grained.
2) Attestation example: attached is a redacted PDF attestation that includes a signed manifest and SHA256 checksums. Signature is an RSA-4096 signature over the manifest and we can provide a chain to verify.
3) 48-hour SLA: This is available as an enterprise addendum. We usually include it in Dedicated/Private contracts for regulated customers; there is an add-on fee tied to our accelerated purge workers and additional support coverage. I'll include sample fee language in the attached DOCX.
4) Logs: Forwarding to customer SIEM within 24 hours and a 7-day purge from Redwood is supported via the log-forwarding configuration. We'll provide Terraform snippets to wire up the sink.

Attachments: sample-sla-data-deletion-clause.docx (contains proposed clause and pricing), redwood-deletion-attestation-example.pdf

If that looks okay I'll put together a short ops & legal call — available slots tomorrow 10:00-11:00 and Thursday 14:00-15:00 PT. Priya, can you coordinate calendar?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
